extracted.intended_audience: NIH extramural research community (investigators, applicants, administrators)
extracted.subtask_description: Collection of NIH news items summarizing recent policy updates, resources, and guidance relevant to preparing and managing NIH grant applications and awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Model selection appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: Investigators should select the models most appropriate for their specific research questions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH supports a wide range of scientifically sound approaches (including New Approach Methodologies, NAMs) to advance understanding of human health and disease, but emphasizes choosing models that enhance human relevance and translational potential and are fit-for-purpose for the research question.

rubrics_metrics.name: PF5 Collaborative International Research Projects: application format and award splitting
rubrics_metrics.description: Key features and application format for the new Collaborative International Research Project (PF5) award structure, including how applications may be split into linked awards after review and before Just-in-Time requests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants should review the 6-minute overview to learn the PF5 structure and how post-review administrative splitting into linked awards can occur; follow the specified PF5 application format.

rubrics_metrics.name: 2026 Pilot Data Management and Sharing (DMS) Plan required elements
rubrics_metrics.description: A new 2026 Pilot DMS Plan format is available based on a simplified set of required elements to use when preparing Data Management and Sharing Plans.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When preparing DMS Plans for eligible submissions, use the 2026 pilot format and include the simplified required elements outlined in the new resource.

rubrics_metrics.name: Replication and reproducibility expectations
rubrics_metrics.description: Embedding replication and reproducibility throughout NIH research is a key priority; reliability of biomedical research is foundational to public trust and patient benefit.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: NIH's Gold Standard Science plan encourages a culture that values replication and reproducibility; NIH has launched a Replication and Reproducibility Initiative to drive, incentivize, and institutionalize these efforts across the biomedical research enterprise. Applicants and awardees should consider replication/reproducibility in applications, study design, and reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring category: 'Competitive but Not Discussed' explained
rubrics_metrics.description: Following emergency modifications, the middle third of applications in a study section were designated as 'competitive but not discussed' recognizing that strong applications may fall below a 33% cut off.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants whose applications are scored as 'competitive but not discussed' should understand this reflects placement in the middle third by the study section under the modified process; consult NIH guidance for implications and next steps.

rubrics_metrics.name: Centralized peer review implementation and effects
rubrics_metrics.description: All peer review was centralized within the Center for Scientific Review (CSR), with intended effects on efficiency, competition, and transparency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The consolidation of peer review is intended to strengthen efficiency, competition, and transparency; applicants should be aware of potential process changes and consult CSR updates for details on how review operations or timelines may be affected.
